summary: Clatsop County, OR lookout: 1920s wooden tower, 1934 replacement, abandoned 1964; a 1986 visit found the tower on the ground; listed as gone.

facts.design: 1957 tower: 65-ft wood tower with 7x7 Amort cab; 1934 tower: 83-ft treated timber with 7x7 L-6 cab (register; Forest Log says 75 ft)
facts.status_note: Abandoned 1964; a 1986 visit found the tower broken up on the ground; both registers list it as gone; no description after 1986 found

events.note: Forest Log (Sept 1934) reports a new 75-ft station with attendant quarters; the register says an 83-ft timber tower replaced the earlier 1920s tower
Donald Kyle put in charge of the new station
After the 1934 tower went up, the old cabin with attached garage was used for storage
65-ft wood tower with 7x7 Amort cab erected
New cabin constructed for the lookout
Abandoned; both registers list the site as gone
Visit found the tower broken up on the ground, most of the cab still on site, tower legs removed, two walls and window frames from the ground cabin, ruins of a cabin nearby

evidence.supports: about nine miles west of Vernonia
first lookout a 60-foot wooden tower and cabin, built in the 1920s
evidence.quote: The first lookout on this site was a 60' wooden tower and cabin built in the 1920s.

evidence.supports: September 1934 new station with a 75-foot tower and attendant quarters
evidence.quote: The tower is 75 feet high, and has been equipped with the most modern fire finding equipment.

evidence.supports: quarters for the attendant built with the 1934 station
evidence.quote: Besides the tower, quarters for the attendant has been built.

evidence.supports: the 1934 station was newly erected on Green Mountain
evidence.quote: The latest lookout station to be added to the list has been erected on Green Mountain

evidence.supports: register gives the 1934 tower 83 feet, a 7x7 L-6 cab and a 14x14 L-4 cabin for living quarters
evidence.quote: In 1934, that was replaced with an 83' treated timber tower with a 7'x7' L-6 cab and a 14'X14' L-4 cabin living quarters.

evidence.supports: Donald Kyle put in charge of the new station
evidence.quote: Donald Kyle has been put in charge of this latest station.

evidence.supports: 65-foot wood tower with 7x7 Amort cab erected in 1957
evidence.quote: 1957: A 65-foot wood tower with a 7x7 Amort cab was erected.
1957: Constructed a new cabin for Green Mountain Lookout.

evidence.supports: old cabin with attached garage used for storage after the 1934 tower
evidence.quote: The abandoned old cabin with attached garage was then used for storage.
The lookout was abandoned in 1964 and is now gone.

evidence.supports: the March 28, 1986 visit found the tower broken up on the ground
evidence.quote: March 28, 1986: A visit found the lookout tower broken up on the ground.

evidence.supports: most of the cab still on site and the tower legs removed
evidence.quote: Most of the cab was still on site, however the tower legs had been removed.

evidence.supports: two walls and window frames from the 14 by 14 ground cabin on site
evidence.quote: Also on the site were two walls and window frames from the 14 x 14 hip-roofed ground cabin.
Nearby were ruins of a cabin.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 83 feet for the 1934 tower; the Forest Lookouts page quotes The Forest Log as saying 75 feet. Both are kept and the story gives both.
The register gives a 7x7 L-6 cab on the 1934 tower and a 14x14 L-4 cabin for living quarters. firelookout.com gives only an L-4 cab for 1934. The register's fuller description is used.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 19.8 equals 65 ft, the 1957 tower on the Forest Lookouts page; the register's 83-ft 1934 tower is the other height, so the record height is ambiguous. Not corrected; the design field names both. The 1920s first tower has no exact year, so it has no built event. Facts.staffing and facts.access are left out: no source gives a staffing status after 1934 or any access rule. The story's 'no source says whether the site is open' sentence is a statement about the sources and has no quote. Do not confuse this with the other Clatsop County Green Mountain (46.01858, -123.70545, tower gone) or with the Forest Lookouts green-mountain2 page, which describes a different BLM lookout. No photos found.
